sections.title: Article heading
sections.text:
ARTICLE 771.

PD 771.

sections.title: Legislative History
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-771.101. LEGISLATIVE HISTORY.

PD 771 was established by Ordinance No.27004, passed by the Dallas City Council on November 12, 2007. (Ord. 27004)

sections.title: Property Location And Size
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-771.102. PROPERTY LOCATION AND SIZE.

PD 771 is established on property located on the south line of Lovers Lane, west of Inwood Road and east of Linwood Avenue. The size of PD 771 is approximately 6.5455 acres. (Ord. 27004)

sections.title: Creation Of Tracts
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-771.103. CREATION OF TRACTS.

This district is divided into five tracts: Tracts I, II, III, IV, and V, as shown on the development plan (Exhibit 771A). (Ord. 27004)

sections.title: Definitions And Interpretations
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-771.104. DEFINITIONS AND INTERPRETATIONS.

(a) Unless otherwise stated, the definitions and interpretations in Chapter 51A apply to this article.

(b) Unless otherwise stated, all references to articles, divisions, or sections in this article are to articles, divisions, or sections in Chapter 51A.

(c) Tracts I, II, and V are considered to be nonresidential zoning districts. Tracts III and IV are considered to be residential zoning districts. (Ord. 27004)

sections.title: Exhibits
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-771.105. EXHIBITS.

The following exhibits are incorporated into this article:

(1) Exhibit 771A: development plan.

(2) Exhibit 771B: landscape plan.

(3) Exhibit 771C: traffic management plan. (Ord. 27004)

sections.title: Development Plan
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-771.106. DEVELOPMENT PLAN.

(a) For a private school, child-care facility, or surface parking use, development and use of the Property must comply with the development plan. If there is a conflict between the text of this article and the development plan, the text of this article controls.

(b) For all other uses, no development plan is required, and the provisions of Section 51A- 4.702 regarding submission of or amendments to a development plan, site analysis plan, conceptual plan, development schedule, and landscape plan do not apply. (Ord. 27004)

sections.title: Main Uses Permitted
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-771.107. MAIN USES PERMITTED.

(a) Tract I.

(1) Except as provided in this subsection, the only main uses permitted in Tract I are those main uses permitted in the CR Community Retail District, subject to the same conditions applicable in the CR Community Retail District, as set out in Chapter 51A. For example, a use permitted in the CR Community Retail District only by specific use permit (SUP) is permitted in this tract only by SUP; a use subject to development impact review (DIR) in the CR Community Retail District is subject to DIR in this tract; etc.

(2) The following main uses are permitted subject to any conditions noted:

-- Child-care facility. -- Private school. [Limited to pre-kindergarten through eighth grade.] -- Surface parking.

(b) Tracts II and V.

(1) Except as provided in this subsection, the only main uses permitted in Tracts II and V are those main uses permitted in the R-7.5(A) Single Family District, subject to the same conditions applicable in the R-7.5(A) Single Family District, as set out in Chapter 51A. For example, a use permitted in the R-7.5(A) Single Family District only by specific use permit (SUP) is permitted in these tracts only by SUP; a use subject to development impact review (DIR) in the R-7.5(A) Single Family District is subject to DIR in these tracts; etc.

(2) The following main uses are permitted subject to any conditions noted:

-- Child-care facility. -- Financial institution with drive-in window. [SUP] -- Financial institution without drive-in window. -- Medical clinic or ambulatory surgical center. -- Office. -- Private school. [Limited to pre-kindergarten through eighth grade.]

(c) Tracts III and IV.

(1) Except as provided in this subsection, the only main uses permitted in Tracts III and IV are those main uses permitted in the R-7.5(A) Single Family District, subject to the same conditions applicable in the R-7.5(A) Single Family District, as set out in Chapter 51A. For example, a use permitted in the R-7.5(A) Single Family District only by specific use permit (SUP) is permitted in these tracts only by SUP; a use subject to development impact review (DIR) in the R-7.5(A) Single Family District is subject to DIR in these tracts; etc.

(2) The following main uses are permitted subject to any conditions noted:

-- Child-care facility. -- Private school. [Limited to pre-kindergarten through eighth grade.]

-- Surface parking. [Tract III only.] (Ord. 27004)

sections.title: Accessory Uses
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-771.108. ACCESSORY USES.

(a) As a general rule, an accessory use is permitted in any district in which the main use is permitted. Some specific accessory uses, however, due to their unique nature, are subject to additional regulations in Section 51A-4.217. For more information regarding accessory uses, consult Section 51A- 4.217.

(b) Athletic field use is allowed in Tracts II and V as an accessory use, but use of the fields is limited to private school or child-care facility uses. (Ord. 27004)

sections.title: Yard, Lot, And Space Regulations
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-771.109. YARD, LOT, AND SPACE REGULATIONS.

(Note: The yard, lot, and space regulations in this section must be read together with the yard, lot, and space regulations in Division 51A-4.400. If there is a conflict between this section and Division 51A- 4.400, this section controls.)

(a) In general. Except as provided in this section, the yard, lot, and space regulations for the CR Community Retail District apply in Tracts I and II, and the yard, lot, and space regulations for the R- 7.5(A) Single Family District apply in Tracts III, IV, and V.

(b) Front yard. For a private school or child-care facility use, minimum front yard is as follows:

(1) Tracts I, II, III, and V: 10 feet.

(2) Tract IV: 35 feet.

(c) Side and rear yard. For a private school or child-care facility use, minimum side and rear yards are as follows:

(1) Except as provided in Paragraph (3), five feet on Tract I.

(2) Except as provided in Paragraph (3), 10 feet on Tracts III, IV, and V.

(3) No minimum side or rear yard is required between tracts.

(d) Floor area. For a private school or child-care facility use, maximum floor area is 114,379 square feet.

(e) Height.

(1) Residential proximity slope. Except as provided in this paragraph, if any portion of a structure is over 32 feet in height, that portion may not be located above a 1:3 residential proximity slope originating in an R, R(A), D, D(A), TH, or TH(A) district, or a 1:1 residential proximity slope originating in a CH, MF-1, MF-1(A), MF-2, or MF-2(A) district. Except for chimneys, structures listed in Section 51A-4.408(a)(2) may project through the slope to a height not to exceed the maximum structure height, or 12 feet above the slope, whichever is less. Chimneys may project through the slope to a height 12 feet above the slope and 12 feet above the maximum structure height.

(2) Height. Except as provided in this subsection and as shown on the development plan, for a private school or child-care facility use, maximum structure height is 54 feet, except that bell towers may project a maximum of 14 feet above the maximum structure height.

(f) Lot coverage. For a private school or child-care facility use, maximum lot coverage is 60 percent. For the purpose of calculating lot coverage, Tracts III, IV, and V are considered to be one lot. Surface parking lots and underground parking structures are not included in lot coverage calculations.

(g) Stories.

(1) For residential uses, maximum number of stories above grade is two.

(2) For all other uses, maximum number of stories above grade is three. (Ord. 27004)

sections.title: Off-Street Parking And Loading
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-771.110. OFF-STREET PARKING AND LOADING.

(a) Consult the use regulations in Division 51A-4.200 for the specific off-street parking and loading requirements for each use.

(b) Aboveground parking structures are prohibited.

(c) For a private school or child-care facility use, parking may be located in the front yard.

(d) For a private school or child-care facility use, this district is considered to be one lot for the off-street parking and loading requirements. (Ord. 27004)

sections.title: Environmental Performance Standards
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-771.111. ENVIRONMENTAL PERFORMANCE STANDARDS.

See Article VI. (Ord. 27004)

sections.title: Landscaping And Tree Mitigation
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-771.112. LANDSCAPING AND TREE MITIGATION.

(a) Private school, child-care facility, or surface parking use.

(1) In general. Except as provided in this section, landscaping must be provided as shown on the landscape plan (Exhibit 771B). If there is a conflict between the text of this article and the landscape plan, the text of this article controls.

(2) When landscaping must be completed.

(A) Except as provided in this subsection, landscaping must be provided for each tract before the final inspection of any structure, addition, or pavement in that tract.

(B) The landscaping and screening in Tracts II and V west of Kaywood Drive must be provided by February 1, 2009. The landscaping in Tract V east of Kaywood Drive must be provided before the final inspection of any structure or addition in that tract.

(3) Tract V screening.

(A) Solid screening must be provided along the west and south property lines in the locations shown on the development plan.

(B) Solid screening must be a minimum of six feet in height measured from the horizontal plane passing through the nearest point of the off-street loading space and must be provided in accordance with Sections 51A-4.602(b)(3)(A), (C), or any combination of (A) or (C).

(C) The landscaping and screening in Tracts II and V west of Kaywood Drive must be provided by February 1, 2009.

(4) Tree mitigation. Tree mitigation must be provided in accordance with Article X, except that trees planted within the parkway adjacent to the Property may count towards any required tree mitigation.

(5) Tree protection. For construction activity within 50 feet of a protected tree, tree protection must be provided in accordance with Article X. Tree protection efforts must be approved by the building official before beginning construction activity.

(6) General maintenance. Plant materials must be maintained in a healthy, growing condition.

(7) Private license granted.

(A) The city council hereby grants a revocable, non-exclusive license to the owners or tenants (with the written consent of the owner) of all property in this district for the exclusive purpose of authorizing trees in the parkway along Kelton Drive. An owner or tenant is not required to pay an initial or annual fee for this license, although a fee may be charged for issuance of a parkway landscape permit. This private license will not terminate at the end of any specific period, however, the city council reserves the right to terminate this license at will, by resolution passed by the city council, any time such termination becomes necessary. The determination by the city council of the need for termination is final and binding. The city shall become entitled to possession of the licensed area without giving any notice and without the necessity of legal proceedings to obtain possession when, in its judgment, the purpose or use of the license is inconsistent with the public use of the right-of-way or when the purpose or use of the license is likely to become a nuisance or a threat to public safety. Upon termination of the license by the city council, each owner or tenant shall remove all improvements and installations in the public rights-of-way to the satisfaction of the director of public works and transportation.

(B) Upon the installation of landscaping and related amenities, such as irrigation systems, in the public rights-of-way, the owner or tenant shall procure, pay for, and keep in full force and effect commercial general liability insurance coverage with an insurance company authorized to do business in the State of Texas and otherwise acceptable to the city, covering, but not limited to, the liability assumed under the private license granted under this paragraph, with combined single limits of liability for bodily injury and property damage of not less than $1,000,000 for each occurrence, and $2,000,000 annual aggregate. Coverage under this liability policy must be on an occurrence basis and the city shall be named as additional insured. Proof of such insurance must be sent to: Office of Risk Management, City of Dallas, 1500 Marilla, Dallas, Texas 75201, and the policy must provide for 30 days prior written notice to the Office of Risk Management of cancellation, expiration, non-renewal, or material change in coverage. All subrogation rights for loss or damage against the city are hereby waived to the extent that they are covered by this liability insurance policy.

(C) Each owner or tenant is responsible for maintaining the landscaping in a healthy, growing condition, for keeping related amenities in good repair and condition, and for keeping

the premises safe and from deteriorating in value or condition, at no expense to the city. The city is absolutely exempt from any requirements to make repairs or to maintain the landscaping, related amenities, or the premises. The granting of a license for landscaping and related amenities under this paragraph does not release the owner or tenant from liability for the installation or maintenance of trees, landscaping, and related amenities in the public right-of-way.

(8) Parkway landscape permit.

(A) It is the responsibility of the property owner to apply for and obtain a parkway landscape permit before locating trees, landscaping, or related amenities in the parkway. An application for a parkway landscape permit must be made to the director. The application must be in writing on a form approved by the director and accompanied by plans or drawings showing the area of the parkway affected and the planting or other amenities proposed.

(B) Upon receipt of the application and any required fees, the director shall circulate it to all affected city departments and utilities for review and comment. If, after receiving comments from affected city departments and utilities, the director determines that the construction, planting, or other amenities proposed will not be inconsistent with and will not unreasonably impair the public use of the right-of-way, the director shall issue a parkway landscape permit to the property owner; otherwise, the director shall deny the permit.

(C) A parkway landscape permit issued by the director is subject to immediate revocation upon written notice if at any time the director determines that the use of the parkway authorized by the permit is inconsistent with or unreasonably impairs the public use of the right- of-way. The property owner is not required to comply with any parkway landscaping requirement of this section if compliance is made impossible due to the director's revocation of a parkway landscape permit.

(D) The issuance of a parkway landscape permit under this paragraph does not excuse the property owner, his agents, or employees from liability for the installation or maintenance of trees or other amenities in the public right-of-way.

(b) All other uses.

(1) Landscaping must be provided in accordance with Article X.

(2) Plant materials must be maintained in a healthy, growing condition. (Ord. 27004)

sections.title: Private  School    And    Child-Care  Facility
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-771.113. PRIVATE SCHOOL AND CHILD-CARE FACILITY ENROLLMENT AND PHASING OF IMPROVEMENTS.

(a) Until a traffic study has been submitted and the director has determined that it is sufficient pursuant to Section 51P-771.115(d), enrollment in a private school or child-care facility may not exceed 485, and no building permits may be issued for buildings, including modular classroom buildings, in the areas shown on the development plan as future building area and potential location for future modular buildings.

(b) After a traffic study has been submitted and the director has determined that it is sufficient pursuant to Section 51P-771.115(d), enrollment in a private school or child-care facility may not exceed 600, and maximum total number of students permitted at the private school or child-care facility at one time is 560 students.

(c) This section does not impair the ability of the city plan commission or city council to call a public hearing on its own motion for the purpose of passing an amending ordinance to address the maximum enrollment permitted for a private school or child-care facility. (Ord. 27004)

sections.title: Signs
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-771.114. SIGNS.

(a) Tracts I, II, and V. Signs must comply with the provisions for business zoning districts in Article VII.

(b) Tracts III and IV. Signs must comply with the provisions for non-business zoning districts in Article VII. (Ord. 27004)

sections.title: Traffic Management Plan
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-771.115. TRAFFIC MANAGEMENT PLAN.

(a) In general. The operation of the private school or child care facility must comply with this section and the traffic management plan (Exhibit 771C).

(b) Queuing. Queuing is only permitted inside the Property. Student drop-off and pick-up are not permitted within city rights-of-way.

(c) Completion date. Drive A, Drive B, and the queue lanes shown on the traffic management plan must be completed by January 31, 2008.

(d) Traffic study.

(1) The property owner or operator shall prepare a traffic study evaluating the sufficiency of the traffic management plan. The initial traffic study must be submitted to the director on or before April 1, 2008. After the initial traffic study, the property owner or operator shall submit annual updates of the traffic study to the director by November 1st of each year.

(2) The traffic study must be in writing, based on a minimum of four samples taken on different school days at different drop-off and pick-up times over a two-week period, and must contain an analysis of the following:

(A) ingress and egress points;

(B) queue lengths;

(C) number and location of personnel assisting with loading and unloading of students;

(D) drop-off and pick-up locations;

(E) drop-off and pick-up hours for each grade level;

(F) hours for each grade level; and

(G) circulation.

(3) Within 30 days after submission of a traffic study, the director shall determine if the current traffic management plan is sufficient.

(A) If the director determines that the current traffic management plan is sufficient, the director shall notify the applicant in writing.

(B) If the director determines that the current traffic management plan results in traffic hazards or traffic congestion, the director shall require the property owner to submit an amended traffic management plan. If the property owner fails to submit an amended traffic management plan within 30 days, the director shall notify the city plan commission and city council for consideration of appropriate zoning amendments, including reducing enrollment to a level that will be accommodated by the queuing system.

(e) Amendment process.

(1) The traffic management plan is part of the development plan. The traffic management plan may be amended by submitting the minor plan amendment fee in Section 51A- 1.105(k)(3) and by following the public hearing process for a minor plan amendment in Section 51A- 4.702(h).

(2) The city plan commission shall authorize changes in a traffic management plan if the proposed amendments improve queuing or traffic circulation, eliminate traffic hazards, or decrease traffic congestion.

(f) Ingress and egress for a private school, child-care facility, or surface parking use.

(1) Tract I. Egress onto Caillet Street is limited to northbound egress only.

(2) Tracts III and IV. Egress is limited to northbound egress only. No southbound egress is permitted. Signs to direct traffic must be provided as shown on the traffic management plan.

(3) Tract V.

(A) Drive A is limited to ingress only.

(B) Drive B is limited to egress only. (Ord. Nos. 27004; 27322)

sections.title: Controlled Access Gate At Kelton Drive And
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-771.116. CONTROLLED ACCESS GATE AT KELTON DRIVE AND KAYWOOD DRIVE.

(a) For a private school or child-care facility use, vehicular traffic through the controlled access gate, shown on the development plan, is limited to emergency vehicles (police, fire, etc.) and trash pick-up.

(b) Trash pick-up is limited to the hours between 8:00 a.m. and 5:00 p.m.

(c) Trash pick-up is permitted through the controlled access gate until August 15, 2008. (Ord. 27004)

sections.title: Exterior Lighting
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-771.117. EXTERIOR LIGHTING.

(a) Exterior lighting. Exterior lighting must comply with the lighting provisions in Section 51A-4.301(e).

(b) Lighting fixtures. All lighting fixtures must be hooded and shielded, and lighting must be directed vertically downward.

(c) Athletic field lighting.

(1) For athletic events, lighting of athletic fields is permitted Monday through Thursday until 9:00 p.m.

(2) For non-athletic events, lighting of athletic fields is permitted a maximum of six days for each calendar year only until 9:30 p.m. (Ord. 27004)

sections.title: Fencing And Visibility Obstruction Regulations
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-771.118. FENCING AND VISIBILITY OBSTRUCTION REGULATIONS.

(a) Fencing.

(1) For a private school or child-care facility use, fencing may be located in the front yard and may not exceed seven-and-one-half feet in height. Fencing must be provided in the location shown on the development plan and landscape plan.

(2) For all other uses, fencing is prohibited in the front yard.

(b) Visibility triangle for a private school, child-care facility, or surface parking use.

(1) Parking in Tract III is permitted in the visibility triangle.

(2) The visibility obstruction regulations in Section 51A-4.602(d) do not apply to Drive A in Tract V. (Ord. 27004)

sections.title: Modular Classroom Buildings
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-771.119. MODULAR CLASSROOM BUILDINGS.

(a) For a private school or child-care facility use, modular classroom buildings are permitted in the locations shown on the development plan.

(b) Modular classroom buildings are permitted only after the issuance of a building permit for any structure or addition in Tract IV or V.

(c) Modular classroom buildings must be removed within two years after the issuance of a building permit for any structure or addition in Tract IV or V, or 90 days after the final inspection for any structure or addition in Tract IV or V, whichever event occurs first. (Ord. 27004)

sections.title: Additional Provisions
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-771.120. ADDITIONAL PROVISIONS.

(a) The Property must be properly maintained in a state of good repair and neat appearance.

(b) Development and use of the Property must comply with all federal and state laws and regulations, and with all ordinances, rules, and regulations of the city.

(c) Permanent outdoor speakers and amplifiers are prohibited. (Ord. 27004)

sections.title: Compliance With Conditions
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-771.121. COMPLIANCE WITH CONDITIONS.

(a) All paved areas, permanent drives, streets, and drainage structure, if any, must be constructed in accordance with standard city specifications, and completed to the satisfaction of the director of public works and transportation.

(b) The building official shall not issue a building permit to authorize work, or a certificate of occupancy to authorize the operation of a use, in this district until there has been full compliance for that use with this article, the Dallas Development Code, the construction codes, and all other ordinances, rules, and regulations of the city. (Ord. 27004)

sections.title: Zoning Map
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-771.122. ZONING MAP.

PD 771 is located on Zoning Map No. G-6. (Ord. 27004)
